title: Booking and client app for independent and mobile dog groomers
subtitle: Quick idea check: is a MoeGo alternative for solo and mobile groomers worth building for a solo iOS developer?

founder.channel: online, plus partner's groomer Facebook groups

verdict.summary: The pain is real but narrow. About 15 different groomers in App Store reviews complain about slow, buggy apps on the road, wrong addresses, metered texts and payment fees, and charges after cancelling. But a general 'cheaper MoeGo' is already taken: MoeGo is well rated, and ZendPaw ($39) and BooknBuddy (from $29.99) already pitch solo groomers and MoeGo switchers. Only build if the speed-on-the-road angle passes a 10-groomer interview test first. Evidence comes from App Store reviews only; Reddit, Capterra, G2 and Trustpilot were blocked.

opportunities.name: Booking + client app for independent/mobile groomers
opportunities.one_liner: Scheduling, client and pet records, reminders and payments for solo groomers.
opportunities.why: pain 6: different groomers repeat the same complaints and some cancel (e9, e11, e12, e18, e5), but all of it comes from one source type, and MoeGo averages 4.59 across 297 ratings, so it stays out of 7+. willingness_to_pay 7: they already pay $49+ and complain about price and fees, not about paying at all (e1, e2, e3, e4, e24). competition_gap 3: a well-liked leader (e21, e22, e23) plus cheap solo plans aimed at MoeGo switchers (e26, e27, e31). founder_fit 6: a phone-first app suits a Swift developer, but matching the leaders needs payments, SMS, web booking and import (e24, e25). reachability 6: the partner's groomer Facebook groups (not checked), a MoeGo users' Facebook group (e34), and public App Store reviews. build_cost 5: matching the leaders is months of work at 12 hours a week.

gap.statement: Solo mobile groomers who work from a van can't get a scheduling app that stays fast and gets addresses right on the road at a flat price, because the leading apps stall mid-route, send them to the wrong address, and charge extra for texts and payments.

pains.theme: Slow and buggy on the road, wrong addresses
pains.summary: Mobile groomers pull over waiting for the app, get sent to wrong addresses, or lose appointments.
Charges continue after cancel or pause; deposits and withdrawals don't add up.

pains.theme: Overpriced, metered texts and payment fees
pains.summary: Paying extra for texts and a 3-5% payment fee feels like too much for what the app does.

pains.theme: Painful setup and import, support fades
pains.summary: Weeks of setup, failed imports lead to cancelling, and support goes quiet after signup.

competitors.name: MoeGo
competitors.pricing: Mobile: $49/mo Basic, $99/mo per van Growth; SMS capped on lower tiers
competitors.positioning: The all-in-one solution for solo groomers with simple operations.
strengths: Well rated: 4.59 across 297 App Store ratings; 35 of the 50 most recent reviews are 5-star

competitors.name: DaySmart Pet
competitors.pricing: Base price not captured from the pricing page; paid add-ons; 14-day trial
competitors.positioning: Long-standing salon and pet business suite.
strengths: Large installed base (1,099 App Store ratings)

competitors.name: BooknBuddy
competitors.pricing: Revenue-tiered: $29.99/mo up to $3,000 revenue, up to $149.99
competitors.positioning: MoeGo alternative whose price drops in slow months.

competitors.name: Pawfinity
competitors.positioning: For grooming, boarding, daycare, training, therapy, and more.

competitors.name: Groomer.io
competitors.pricing: Not shown on the fetched page
competitors.positioning: Software and websites purpose-built for grooming salons and mobile groomers.
weaknesses: No US App Store reviews returned

critic.risk: Crowded at the low end: ZendPaw ($39) and BooknBuddy ($29.99) already sell cheap solo plans and target MoeGo switchers, so 'cheaper MoeGo' is not a gap.
MoeGo is well liked: 4.59 across 297 ratings, with most recent reviews 5-star.
critic.rebuttal: Partly. The complaints that do exist cluster on speed and addresses while mobile (e9, e11, e12), a narrow angle MoeGo's marketing doesn't lead with. That is a hypothesis to test, not a proven gap.

critic.risk: A free generic substitute (Square Free) exists.
critic.rebuttal: Not grooming-specific: no pet records or routing (e30).

critic.risk: Switching cost: client and pet history is hard to move, and a failed import made a groomer cancel.
critic.rebuttal: Doing the import by hand for the first users turns this into an offer (e18).

critic.risk: iOS-only leaves out Android groomers, and their clients will need a web booking page anyway.
Someone tried and died: the search found no shutdowns.
critic.rebuttal: No dead competitors found; the market is alive and crowded instead.

win_plan.positioning: The grooming app that doesn't make you pull over: fast on the road, addresses that are right, one flat price with texts included.

switching_triggers.move: One-tap cancel, a written no-charge-after-cancel promise
Offline-first day view the partner can demo in a van
Flat price including texts; use any card processor

offers: Hand-done import from MoeGo or DaySmart
Cancel in one tap, never charged after

build_first.feature: Offline day route and client card

where_to_find.why: Direct access through the partner; check each group's self-promotion rules
Mentioned by a reviewer (e34); not opened

pricing.recommendation: $29/mo flat including texts, only if the interviews pass
pricing.competitor_range: $29.99 (BooknBuddy entry) to $49 (MoeGo mobile Basic), $99+ per van
pricing.rationale: The low end is already at $30-39, so price can't be the wedge. Texts included and no processor lock-in are the differences.

validation.experiment: Your partner interviews 10 solo mobile groomers from their Facebook groups: current app, all-in monthly cost, top 2 annoyances. No pitch and no links.
validation.pass_bar: 6 of 10 name speed or addresses on the road among their top 2 annoyances, AND 3 say they'd switch for $29 flat with import done for them, AND fewer than half are already happy on ZendPaw, BooknBuddy or similar
steps: Day 1-2: partner posts a no-link question in 3 groups, books 10 calls
Day 3-5: calls, log answers in a sheet
Day 6: ask the 3 most interested for a $29 pre-order or a migration slot
Day 7: score against the pass bar

kill_criteria: Fewer than 6 of 10 rank on-the-road speed or addresses in their top 2
Most are already happy with a $30-40 alternative
